short: Vacancy-Driven Gelation Using Defect-Rich Nanoassemblies of
title: Vacancy-Driven Gelation Using Defect-Rich Nanoassemblies of 2D Transition Metal Dichalcogenides and Polymeric Binder for Biomedical Applications

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Pristine 2D MoS2 has few planar defects and lacks active centres for conjugating polymer chains. Defect-rich MoS2 nanoassemblies should crosslink four-arm PEG-SH into a hydrogel through vacancy active centres.
states.detail: Absorbed: h1 (HYP/gap), h2 (HYP/hypothesis), d1 (DES/base_system), d2 (DES/variable_sweep), d3 (DES/variable_sweep), p1 (PRC/synthesis), p2 (PRC/synthesis)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Atomic vacancy (defect-site) density of MoS2 rises with thiourea ratio from 1:1 to 1:6. PEG thiols chemisorb at MoS2 vacancy sites, forming C-S-Mo crosslinks
states.detail: Absorbed: s3 (STR/defect/point), s4 (STR/chemistry/bonding). Premises: Raman A1g/E12g ratio and defect-related PL emission track defect and unsaturated-atom content in MoS2; Raman bands at ~670 and ~2570 cm-1 are S-H deformation and S-H stretching of thiols

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Vacancy sites act as active centres binding thiol ends, so each nanoassembly links many PEG arms into a network. MoS2 addition turns PEG-SH solution into a gel (G' rises by 4 decades); PEG-SH alone stays sol.
states.detail: Absorbed: m1 (MEC/pathway), r1 (PRP/value), r2 (PRP/value). Premises: Thiols bind strongly to Mo at sulfur-vacancy sites of MoS2

states.title: Performance state
states.head: Gel forms in cell culture medium faster and stiffer: G' ~1e4 Pa within 90 min vs ~1.7 kPa after 400 min in water. Cells encapsulated during vacancy-driven gelation survive with high viability (>85%)

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Defect-rich MoS2 nanoassemblies crosslink PEG-SH by vacancy-driven chemisorption into stiff, elastic, cytocompatible hydrogels for cell delivery
